summary: Leo Meyer was a linguist who studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and at Berlin under Jacob Grimm, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Göttingen (1862–1865; chair in 1898) and Tartu/Dorpat (1865–1899).
Leo Rishi Nelson Jones works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a project staff member (attested 2026).

Leo Strauss was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Marburg, Freiburg, and Columbia. His academic appointments included Cambridge (~1934–1937), The New School (~1938–1949), University of Chicago (~1949–1968), Claremont McKenna College (~1968–1969), and St. John's College (~1969–1973).
Leon Hurvitz worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He served as a professor at the University of Washington (~1955–1971) and at the University of British Columbia (~1971–1992).

Linguist Leonard Bloomfield studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago under Francis Asbury Wood, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Illinois (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), Chicago (1927–1940), and Yale as Sterling Professor of Linguistics (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Leiden University (~1970–1977) and later served on its faculty from 1998 to 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under F. E. L. Priestley and doctoral supervisor A. K. Warder, and held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).

Religious studies scholar Leonard Swidler studied at St. Norbert College, Marquette, Wisconsin-Madison, Tübingen, and Munich. After teaching at Duquesne University (1960–1966), he was Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).

id: P:Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp
summary: Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held posts at the University of Washington (~1987–1995) and Harvard University (1995).
Leonid Kulikov is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who has held posts at Leiden University (attested 2007) and Ghent University (attested 2026).

Leopold Pospisil studied law at Charles University, sociology at Willamette University, and anthropology at the University of Oregon and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale (from 1956) and curator at the Peabody Museum (~1956–1993).

Indologist Leopold von Schroeder studied at Tartu/Dorpat under Leo Meyer, as well as at Jena and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Tartu (1882, 1890), Innsbruck (1896), and the University of Vienna (1899).

Leslie S. Kawamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther. He spent his career as a professor at the University of Calgary (~1976–2010).

Scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies Levi McLaughlin studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University. He held positions at Kokugakuin University, University of Iowa, and North Carolina State University (from 2012).

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel's MA supervision and held posts at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and University of Bonn (attested 2021).

Lewis Hodous was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Case Western Reserve, Hartford Seminary, and Halle-Wittenberg. He served as president of Foochow Union Theological School (1902–1912, 1914–1917) and professor at Hartford Seminary (1917–1945).

Lewis Lancaster studied at Roanoke, Claremont, and Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Sinology, he held appointments at the University of California, Berkeley (~1967–2002) and as president of the University of the West (1992).

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the China Society of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center (2000).

Lhakpa Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who has held posts as Professor at Tibet University and Assistant Professor of Tibetan Language and Literature at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).
